title: Hexagonal lattice shells form as silica collects in grooves between surface vesicles

fields.label: Label
fields.value: Hexagonal lattice shells form as silica collects in grooves between surface vesicles

fields.label: Statement
fields.value: When the outer surface of a radiolarian is covered by a layer of nearly equal froth-like vesicles, silica secreted or adsorbed at the surface collects in the grooves between them, producing a spherical shell of rods in a regular hexagonal network; less regular vesicles give less regular meshes, and repeated layers give concentric shells.

fields.label: Chapter
fields.value: Ch. IX: On Concretions, Spicules, and Spicular Skeletons

fields.label: Quotation
fields.value: it will at once follow that they will show a tendency to aggregate in the grooves which separate the vesicles, and the result will be the development of a most delicate sphere composed of tiny rods arranged in a regular hexagonal network

fields.label: Agent
fields.value: delphisci On Growth and Form claim extractor

fields.label: Assumptions
fields.value: D’Arcy Wentworth Thompson, On Growth and Form (1st ed., Cambridge: Cambridge University Press, 1917), Chapter IX, “On Concretions, Spicules, and Spicular Skeletons”; topic “Radiolarian lattice shells”. Scope: spherical lattice-shelled Radiolaria (e.g. Aulonia, Actinomma, Cenosphaera)

fields.label: Assessment
fields.value: GPT-5.6 Sol on thompson1917-ch09-14: needs-new-data, resolvability 0.49

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: The mechanism gives clear spatial and correlational predictions. Public imaging may describe mature shells, but matched developmental vesicle and silica maps across the named taxa are unlikely to be adequate.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Co-register developing vesicle boundaries and silica deposition in 3D and quantify whether rods arise specifically in intervesicular grooves, with mesh regularity tracking vesicle size variance and layers tracking repeated vesicle shells. Alternative cytoskeletal templates should be compared.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Adult lattice geometry does not uniquely reveal the deposition template.

Suitable live or staged radiolarian ultrastructure is rare.

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: Mesh statistics are a direct geometric test and radiolarian lattices are extensively imaged in an open taxonomic system. The developmental step, silica collecting in grooves between vesicles, is not in those images. Hexagonal order can therefore support the form prediction for a well-illustrated subset of species while leaving the groove mechanism interchangeable with other pattern-forming processes.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: On spherical lattice shells, measure the fraction of hexagonal meshes, node angles near 120 degrees, and whether irregularity of the mesh tracks irregularity that a vesicular foam would produce. Strong hexagonal order is consistent with groove collection; a different predominant polygon, or order unrelated to any foam, counts against that route.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Hexagonal nets are also expected from other physical models, including bubble packing and reaction-diffusion.

Finished skeletons do not preserve the surface vesicles that supposedly moulded the grooves.
